context: Hiroshi-elder takes a quiet bus ride; chats with Sho-young about it.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 先日、バスで、長く立っとってん。
lines.en: The other day I was standing on the bus for quite a while.
lines.style: Slow, measured cadence with Kansai accent. Warm, fond reminiscence in the voice — like settling into a memory. Gentle weight on each word, no rush. The kind of telling that invites listening.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: おじいちゃん、どうして座らなかったの?
lines.en: Grandpa, why didn't you sit down?
lines.style: Genuinely curious, not challenging. Soft, engaged tone. Small voice with real concern underneath — the kind of question a child asks when they're trying to understand something important. Leans forward slightly in attention.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 途中、お年寄り、譲ってあげたんや。
lines.en: Along the way, an elderly person got on, so I gave up my seat.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact delivery with understated gentleness. Kansai rhythm, unhurried. No self-congratulation — just stating what happened. Warm but humble, like it was the obvious thing to do.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: えらい!靴、疲れなかった?
lines.en: That's wonderful! Didn't your feet get tired?
lines.style: Genuine awe and admiration in the tone. Soft, wondering — Sho recognizing something good without fully understanding why it's good yet. Tender concern for the grandfather's comfort mixed with respect. Slightly breathless with care.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: カード、ピッ、で降りてん。
lines.en: I just tapped my card and got off the bus.
lines.style: Light, casual tone with a hint of Kansai warmth. The practicality of ending the day, matter-of-fact but not dismissive. A small smile in the voice — the simplicity of how it all worked out.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: せいせいするね、人助けで。
lines.en: It feels nice, helping someone like that.
lines.style: Soft, genuine appreciation. No performance — Sho speaking what he's actually feeling. A kind of quiet joy in discovering something true about the world. Gentle, thoughtful, slightly wondering still.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ふふ、お前も、優しい子になれ。
lines.en: Heh. You grow up to be kind like that too, all right?
lines.style: Soft, affectionate chuckle opening the line. Kansai lilt underneath. Tender, gentle instruction — not commanding but gently steering. The voice of someone who sees goodness in a child and wants to nurture it. Quiet weight of hope in the closing.
